nodes.title: A missing reservation
nodes.text: It is 11:30 p.m. You paid for two nights at the hotel and have a confirmation email. The receptionist cannot find a reservation under your surname.
nodes.question: What is an effective first step before making another payment?

choices.label: Show the confirmation email and ask the receptionist to search its booking number.
choices.feedback: The booking number leads to your paid reservation under your middle name.

choices.label: Ask whether the reservation was entered under your full name, including your middle name.
choices.feedback: The name search finds two similar records. The receptionist now needs a unique reference.

choices.label: Reserve another room now and leave the original payment for tomorrow.
choices.feedback: A second reservation would create another charge. The original paid booking has not been checked yet.

nodes.title: Two similar names
nodes.text: The receptionist finds two guests with similar full names. Both arrive tonight. You still have your confirmation email.
nodes.question: Which response reliably identifies your own reservation?

choices.label: Give the booking number from the email and ask them to match it.
choices.feedback: The unique booking number identifies your reservation, so the receptionist can check its details.

choices.label: Accept the first record because the surname and arrival date match.
choices.feedback: A matching name and date do not distinguish the two bookings. The receptionist cannot safely check you into that record.

nodes.title: Before a second charge
nodes.text: The receptionist offers a new reservation, but it would charge your card again. Your original confirmation shows that payment was received.
nodes.question: How can you recover the situation without paying twice?

choices.label: Pause the new payment and ask them to trace the paid booking using the confirmation number.
choices.feedback: You stop the second charge in time. The receptionist locates the original paid booking.

choices.label: Authorise the new payment without checking whether the first booking can be used.
choices.feedback: The new booking is charged while the original payment is still unresolved. You now have two charges to sort out.

nodes.title: Check the stay
nodes.text: Your paid reservation has been found. The receptionist offers a key and says you will check out tomorrow. Your confirmation is for two nights, with checkout the following day.
nodes.question: Which response resolves the remaining mismatch before you take the key?

choices.label: Point to the two-night dates in the email and ask them to confirm the checkout date.
choices.feedback: The receptionist corrects the checkout date and confirms both paid nights before handing over the key.

choices.label: Take the key and assume the checkout date will correct itself overnight.
choices.feedback: The record still shows checkout tomorrow. Taking the key has not resolved the missing second night.

choices.label: Ask whether breakfast is included without mentioning the checkout date.
choices.feedback: You get the breakfast information, but the checkout mismatch remains. The receptionist asks whether tomorrow is the right departure date.

nodes.title: One more chance to clarify
nodes.text: The receptionist asks, 'So you leave tomorrow?' Your email shows a two-night stay. The key is ready, but the dates have not been corrected.
nodes.question: Which reply makes the required correction explicit?

choices.label: Say, 'My confirmation is for two nights. Could you update checkout to the following day?'
choices.feedback: You state the specific mismatch and requested correction. Both nights are now confirmed.

choices.label: Say, 'Yes, that is fine,' and plan to discuss the extra night after checkout.
choices.feedback: Agreeing confirms the wrong departure date. The second night remains unresolved.

nodes.title: Both nights confirmed
nodes.text: You check in using the original payment, with the correct checkout date. You verified the booking and resolved the practical problem.

nodes.title: A night still missing
nodes.text: The booking still ends tomorrow. You reached a room but did not secure the full stay you paid for. Practise again and clarify the dates before accepting the key.

nodes.title: Identity not confirmed
nodes.text: The receptionist cannot safely use someone else's booking. The conversation ends without confirming your reservation.

nodes.title: An avoidable second charge
nodes.text: You have a new room booking, but the original payment remains unresolved. The immediate choice created a second payment problem.
